title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 438
paragraphs: Polycrates, having read this and perceived by reflection that Amasis was giving him good counsel, sought to find which of his treasures he would be most pained in his soul to lose; and in his search he found this, which I shall describe. He had a signet-ring that he used to wear, set in gold and made of an emerald stone; it was the work of Theodoros son of Telecles, of Samos. Seeing that he thought it right to cast this away, he did the following: he manned a fifty-oared galley with sailors and went on board it himself, and then he ordered them to put out into the deep sea. When he had gotten a good distance from the island, he took off the signet-ring, and in sight of all who were with him in the ship, he threw it into the sea. Having done this, he sailed home; and when he came to his house, he mourned for his loss.
